transcript.text: Hi everyone. I'm calling us together for the prebuild review of the Atrium Theater stage plan. As we all know, the dance special films this Friday, and the current draft includes a rotating platform, an overhead lift, floor anchors drilled into the stage, and a two-meter camera lane. Before I can sign off on the final plan, I need us to review all of these elements together as one compatible stage plan. Let's start by having technical, location, and movement staff walk me through any concerns or constraints on each component so we can confirm everything works together.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we go any further. During a camera-rail test I ran, I confirmed that the rotating platform as specified in the current draft would enter the camera lane's required three-meter exclusion zone. The technically approved layout actually requires a fixed platform with a three-meter camera lane — not a rotating platform with a two-meter lane. I recorded this in the technical log, but I haven't yet updated Mara's design draft to reflect it. So the draft you're all looking at does not match what my testing showed is safe and compatible.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical location constraint. I confirmed with the Atrium Theater's preservation officer this morning that drilling into the theater floor is prohibited. The approved replacement requires exactly 18 ballast bases for a freestanding platform. I received the written restriction this morning, but it hasn't been added to the location packet yet, so the draft's floor anchor plan is not viable at this venue.

I reviewed the lead dancer's current medical clearance with the performer and choreographer, and it prohibits overhead lifts for this shoot. The cleared replacement is a floor duet.
